clue.text: Intense as, say, Jack Palance's debut

parts.note: Jack Dee is a British stand-up comedian, so 'as, say, Jack' points to his surname

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so this picks the opening letter of Palance's

parts.note: first letter P

explanation.surface: A remark that something is as intense as the screen debut of the Hollywood tough guy Jack Palance.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Palance looks like one name, but 'Jack' is a different Jack: Jack Dee, a deadpan British comedian. 'as, say,' marks him as an example of a Jack.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep feelings or colours are strong and profound, a straightforward synonym for intense.

clue.text: Q & A about uniform on railway creates a dilemma

indicators.note: the letters of Q and A go around another piece, as if wrapped about it

parts.note: read out in full, Q AND A
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A question-and-answer session about a railway uniform leaves someone stuck for a decision.
explanation.definitionFit: A quandary is a state of perplexity over which of two courses to take, which is what a dilemma is.

clue.text: Jazz age was best, conclusively, for enthusiasm

indicators.note: taking each word at its conclusion, so the final letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Someone nostalgic claims the Jazz Age was the best era for sheer enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is keen relish and energy for something, a near synonym of enthusiasm.

clue.text: Woman visiting South American country with Mike every year

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a place, so the woman's name sits within the country

parts.note: Peru is a country in South America
Ann is a woman's name
M is Mike in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A woman makes an annual trip to a South American country with a man called Mike.
explanation.definitionFit: Per annum is Latin for by the year, used in English for anything happening annually.

clue.text: Tolerate mushroom in a cassoulet on vacation

indicators.note: the mushroom goes inside the remaining letters of cassoulet
vacated means emptied, so cassoulet loses its inside and keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: outer letters C and T
a cep is a porcini mushroom

explanation.surface: Someone puts up with finding a mushroom in the cassoulet while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' sounds like being on holiday, but it means the word cassoulet is emptied to its first and last letters. A cassoulet is a French bean and meat stew.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept something is to put up with it without protest, which is tolerating it.

clue.text: Put Up, Up and Away under film, raising tempo initially, and cause a violent reaction

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits beneath the first
in a down clue, putting a word up means writing it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the word Up written as it appears

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a letter moves it higher, that is earlier in the word

parts.note: to film is to shoot

indicators.note: the initial letter of the word tempo is the one that gets moved

parts.note: first letter T
far means distant or away

explanation.surface: A film title like 'Up, Up and Away' with its tempo raised, causing outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up, Up and Away' reads as a film title, but each word works separately; in a down clue 'Put Up' and 'raising' both refer to moving upwards in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: To push someone too far is to provoke them beyond their limit until they react angrily or violently.

clue.text: Attempt French for the firm

parts.note: to have a stab is to have an attempt
le is the masculine French word for the

explanation.surface: An instruction to try the French language on behalf of a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A stable structure or relationship is steady and secure, the adjectival sense of firm.

clue.text: Summons determination, making good whiskey

indicators.note: the letter for good is made into the letter for whiskey, a substitution

parts.note: grit is courage and determination
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Summoning up determination produces fine whiskey.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a written court order, and a summons ordering someone to appear is a common type.

clue.text: Occasionally, cell buddies escape

indicators.note: taking letters only now and then, at regular intervals, so every other letter of cell buddies

explanation.surface: Prison cellmates sometimes manage a breakout together.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude pursuers is to evade or escape them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Meet nurse to consider medical TV show

parts.note: EN is an Enrolled Nurse
to count someone lucky is to consider them so
ER is the American hospital drama series

explanation.surface: An invitation to meet a nurse and consider a hospital television drama.
explanation.definitionFit: An encounter is a meeting, and as a verb to encounter is to come across or meet.

clue.text: Understand queen's wearing crown lined with fine fabric

indicators.note: a lining sits inside, so the crown word has the other letters inside it

parts.note: the pate is the crown of the head

indicators.note: the queen has the fabric on, wrapped within her letters

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina; the 's reads as 'is'
net is a fine mesh fabric

explanation.surface: A queen wears a crown lined with delicate fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: The fabric is put inside the queen first, and that whole group goes inside the crown. ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the crossword queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To penetrate a mystery is to see into it and grasp its meaning, which is understanding it.

clue.text: In rehab I treated addiction

indicators.note: the answer is contained in the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A recovering addict says their addiction was dealt with in rehab.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug habit is an addiction, the sense of a compulsive dependence.

clue.text: Simple crash involving vehicles blocking bridge

indicators.note: something blocking a bridge sits in the middle of it

parts.note: a span is a bridge or arch
RTA, a road traffic accident

explanation.surface: A simple car crash leaves vehicles blocking a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: RTA (road traffic accident) is the British official term for a vehicle crash.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan living is austere and plain, like the ancient Spartans, hence simple.

clue.text: Less risky returning in the role of whistle-blower after retirement

indicators.note: going back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: as, as in 'acting as captain'

indicators.note: retiring is drawing back, so the referee's letters are read backwards too

parts.note: a ref, or referee, blows a whistle

explanation.surface: A whistle-blower who has retired may feel less at risk in the role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whistle-blower' suggests an informer, but here it is a referee with a whistle. Each of the two pieces is turned around separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Safer is the comparative of safe, meaning carrying less danger or risk.

clue.text: Rotten liar's awful driving

indicators.note: an awful version of the letters is a botched rearrangement of them

parts.note: the letters of rotten liar; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A dreadful liar's driving is awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driving' looks like what the liar does badly, but it is the definition, as in driving rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving rain falls hard and heavily, which is what torrential rain does.

clue.text: Tools cutting right into driers

indicators.note: one letter cuts the other word, slicing into it
into places the cutting letter inside the word for driers

parts.note: towels dry you, so they are driers

explanation.surface: Tools are used to slice straight into drying machines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driers' suggests tumble driers, but here it is towels, things that dry you.
explanation.definitionFit: Trowels are small hand implements for gardening or plastering, examples of tools.

clue.text: Military unit capturing last of enemy with zero authority

indicators.note: the unit holds the captured letter inside it

parts.note: the SAS is the Special Air Service, a British army regiment

indicators.note: the final letter of the word enemy

parts.note: last letter Y
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A special forces unit captures an enemy soldier with no authority to do so.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's say-so is their permission or command, the authority to make something happen.

clue.text: Lobby in favour of fencing Yorkshire's border

indicators.note: a fence encloses, so the first word surrounds the border letters

parts.note: for, as in 'for the motion'
the edges of the word Yorkshire, Y and E

explanation.surface: A lobby group campaigns in favour of putting a fence along the Yorkshire border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lobby' looks like a verb about campaigning, but it is the entrance hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A foyer is the entrance hall of a theatre or hotel, which is a lobby.

clue.text: Excellent soldier leaves coat

indicators.note: the soldier leaves the word, so his letters are removed

parts.note: magic as slang for wonderful or excellent
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An outstanding soldier walks off and leaves his coat behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' could be foliage, but it is the soldier departing from MAGIC. A mac, short for mackintosh, is a raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A mac is a waterproof raincoat, a type of coat.

clue.text: Made merry, when Eddy's almost taken in by rogue

indicators.note: the eddy piece is taken inside the rogue's letters

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a rogue

indicators.note: nearly all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: an eddy is a whirling vortex; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: People had fun when a man called Eddy was nearly conned by a rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eddy' looks like a man's name, but it is a whirlpool.
explanation.definitionFit: To cavort is to leap and prance about in high spirits, which is making merry.

clue.text: Fanta's first, then open Sprite

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word Fanta

parts.note: first letter F
an airy room is open and spacious

explanation.surface: A drinker reaches for a Fanta first and then opens a Sprite.
explanation.walkthrough: Fanta and Sprite look like two fizzy drinks; Sprite is the definition, a supernatural being.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is a small elf-like spirit from folklore, the same as a fairy.

clue.text: TV and papers ousting leader of party before fight

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece comes before, above, the second
the papers push out the first letter of the party word and take its place

parts.note: a riot is a wild party or uproarious time
ID, identity papers
to box is to fight

explanation.surface: Television and the press are pushing aside a party leader ahead of a political fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader of party' looks like a politician, but it is just the first letter of the party word, which the papers replace.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiot box is a jokey slang name for a television set, mocking what it shows.

clue.text: Runs with crazy idea, using rap sheets principally to identify looters

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: crazy letters are jumbled out of their sane order
the principal, that is first, letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Police use criminal records to pin down the looters behind a mad scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' scrambles IDEA to AIDE; rap sheets are criminal records, but here only their initials RS count.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiders who sack a town carry off its goods, so they are plunderers or looters.

clue.text: Cool chopper that could help to get one up a mountain

definitions.text: Cool chopper that could help to get one up a mountain

parts.note: ice is something that cools, or chills
an axe is a chopping tool

explanation.surface: A neat little cutting tool that might help a climber reach a summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopper' suggests a helicopter lifting someone up a mountain, but it is the axe.
explanation.definitionFit: Mountaineers use this pick-like tool to cut steps and arrest falls when climbing on frozen slopes.

clue.text: Field men to support cult

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath the one it holds up

parts.note: a sect is a religious group, a cult
OR, other ranks, the soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: An instruction to send men into the field to back a cult.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is the crossword term for ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A sector is an area of activity, such as the public sector, which is a field.

clue.text: Frightful person drinking vermouth before five brought back dizziness

indicators.note: carried back in the reverse direction, so the whole assembly is read backwards
the ogre takes the vermouth inside

parts.note: an ogre is a frightening person
it is Italian vermouth, as in gin and it
V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A dreadful character downing a vermouth before five o'clock ends up dizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is short for Italian vermouth, as in the drink gin and it. The reversal covers everything built before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is a spinning sensation of giddiness, often from heights, which is dizziness.

clue.text: Stayed in middle of Colditz with English officer

indicators.note: the central letter of a seven-letter word

parts.note: middle letter D
LT is lieutenant

explanation.surface: A prisoner remained inside Colditz with an English officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Colditz was a German castle used as a prisoner-of-war camp for Allied officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwelt is the past tense of dwell, to live or reside somewhere, so it means stayed.

clue.text: What the tabloids call Boris Johnson when Germany replaces British combat training site

indicators.note: joins the nickname to the swap that follows it, setting up the substitution
one letter stands in for the other, a straight substitution

parts.words: What the tabloids call Boris Johnson
parts.note: BoJo is the tabloid nickname for the former UK prime minister
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: A newspaper nickname for Boris Johnson when Germany takes Britain's place.
explanation.definitionFit: A dojo is the hall where judo, karate and other martial arts are taught and practised.

clue.text: Long-lasting stain finally covered by rug — it's coloured

indicators.note: the stain's last letter is hidden under the rug, which takes its place

parts.note: a chronic illness is long-lasting

indicators.note: the final letter of the word stain

parts.note: last letter N
a mat is a small rug

explanation.surface: A persistent stain has been hidden under a rug, which turns out to be colourful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered by' replaces the N in CHRONIC with MAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Chromatic means relating to or having colour, from the Greek chroma, colour.

clue.text: Failed in audition for film

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: missed, as in failed to hit

explanation.surface: An actor flopped at a screen test for a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audition' and 'film' suggest an actor's screen test, but audition means hearing. 'film' is a thin layer, a misty coating.
explanation.definitionFit: A film of condensation on glass is a mist, a thin hazy coating.

clue.text: Drug that's acceptable in church?

indicators.note: the acceptable word goes inside the church letters

parts.note: CE, the Church of England
OK means acceptable

explanation.surface: A question of whether some drug is allowed inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Coke is a slang name for cocaine, a narcotic drug.

clue.text: Put together project, securing vote with an attitude

indicators.note: the projecting word holds the vote mark firmly inside it

parts.note: to jut is to project or stick out
X is the mark made on a ballot paper
a pose is a bodily attitude or stance

explanation.surface: A political project wins a vote while striking an attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'project' looks like a noun, a scheme, but it is the verb, to stick out.
explanation.definitionFit: To juxtapose things is to place them side by side, often for contrast.

clue.text: Start chess, ultimately, with pawn

indicators.note: the ultimate, that is final, letter of chess

parts.note: last letter S
to hock something is to pawn it

explanation.surface: An instruction to open a chess game by moving a pawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pawn' is the chess piece in the surface, but here it is the verb, to pledge something for a loan. 'Start' is the noun, a jolt of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A start is a sudden jump of surprise or alarm, the same as a shock.
